title: Product Usage Scoring & Routing
takeaway: A gated routing policy turns noisy product and intent signals into an inspectable weekly action queue.

scenes.intent: Product usage and intent signals pile up while the weekly queue arrives late or unexplained.
scenes.headline: Signals pile up. The queue stays unexplained.

scenes.intent: One transparent Work Queue turns the signals into routed weekly actions for 120 synthetic accounts.
scenes.headline: One transparent weekly work queue.
scenes.assetAlt: Weekly Sales and Customer Success action queue for 120 synthetic accounts.

scenes.intent: The gated policy qualifies 25, routes 12, and defers 13 at the same capacity as the naive comparator.
scenes.headline: Gated policy: 25 qualify, 12 route, 13 defer.
scenes.assetAlt: Routing policy view comparing a gated policy and a naive score.

scenes.intent: A decision packet shows the explicit intent, route, gates, SLA, and rejected naive alternative for one account.
scenes.headline: Every route explains itself.
scenes.assetAlt: Account decision packet showing scores, gates, route, SLA, and rejected alternative.

scenes.intent: The acquisition intent minimum and weekly capacity are bounded controls; overflow remains visibly deferred.
scenes.headline: Change intent or capacity. See overflow stay deferred.
scenes.assetAlt: Policy view with acquisition intent and weekly human-action capacity controls.

scenes.intent: Invite the viewer to inspect the case study and live demo without claiming validated business efficacy.
scenes.headline: Routing you can inspect.
scenes.assetAlt: Public live-demo capture for Product Usage Scoring and Routing.
